objective_text: Convert improper rational functions before decomposing

questions.stem:
Convert the improper rational function to a proper one by multiplying both the numerator and denominator by the LCD of the terms in the denominator. What is the correct form of the following function?
f(x) = (3x + 6)/(2x^2 - 8x)
questions.solution:
The LCD of the terms in the denominator (2x^2 - 8x) is 2x(x - 4). Multiply both the numerator and denominator by this LCD to get a proper rational function:

f(x) = [(3x + 6) * 2x(x - 4)] / [2x^2 - 8x] * 2x(x - 4)
f(x) = (6x^2 - 12x + 12x - 24) / 4x(x - 4)
f(x) = (6x^2 - 24) / 4x(x - 4)
f(x) = (3x + 6)/(4x(x - 4))
questions.explanation: The correct conversion maintains the equality of the function while making it a proper rational function by removing any common factors between the numerator and denominator.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is not multiplying both the numerator and denominator by the LCD, leading to an incorrect simplified form.
